headline: Jailer 2 Crosses ₹209 Crore Worldwide in Two Days, Eyes a Record Weekend
subheadline: A 38% day-two drop counts as a phenomenal hold for a Rajinikanth opener. With Dussehra holidays ahead, trade trackers say ₹500 crore by midweek is in play.
body:
• Jailer 2 grossed about ₹84 crore worldwide on day two, taking its two-day worldwide total to roughly ₹209 crore, Pinkvilla reported.
  • India gross reached ₹108 crore in two days (₹66.75 crore Thursday, ₹41.25 crore Friday) — a 38% day-two drop that counts as a strong hold for a big South opener.
  • Sacnilk's net figures put India at ₹96.8 crore after two days, with the Hindi version contributing ₹5.5 crore net; Koimoi notes the film is already Kollywood's fifth-highest grosser of 2026 in India.
  • Trade expects ₹100 crore-plus more over Saturday and Sunday, with Dussehra holidays on Monday and Tuesday putting the ₹500 crore mark in play by midweek.

Rajinikanth's Jailer 2 is doing what very few Indian films ever do: holding. The Nelson Dilipkumar sequel collected about ₹41 crore gross in India on its second day — a drop of roughly 38% from its ₹66.75 crore opening day, which trade trackers call a phenomenal hold for a South Indian film that opened this big. Add a stronger overseas day and the film grossed about ₹84 crore worldwide on Friday alone, for a two-day worldwide cumulative of roughly ₹209 crore, Pinkvilla reported.

The numbers, two ways

Gross and net figures differ by tracker, but they tell the same story. Pinkvilla's gross tally has India at ₹108 crore in two days and overseas adding $4.5 million (about ₹43 crore) on day two alone. Sacnilk's net count puts India at ₹96.8 crore after day two (₹37.1 crore net on Friday) and worldwide gross at about ₹210 crore including roughly ₹97 crore overseas. Either way, the film crossed ₹200 crore worldwide in 48 hours — and, per Koimoi, has already become Kollywood's fifth-highest-grossing film of 2026 in India.

"Add a stronger overseas day and the film grossed about ₹84 crore worldwide on Friday alone, for a two-day worldwide cumulative of roughly ₹209 crore, Pinkvilla reported."

The Hindi version is a smaller but steady contributor: it netted ₹5.5 crore in two days, holding well on Friday with ₹2.75 crore, Pinkvilla reported — multiples of the original Jailer's Hindi day-two figure, though well behind Coolie's Hindi pace.

How high can the weekend go?

Pinkvilla projects ₹100 crore-plus worldwide across Saturday and Sunday, which would carry the extended four-day weekend past ₹400 crore — and the calendar keeps helping. Dussehra and Puja holidays fall on Monday and Tuesday, and if the hold continues, the film could close in on ₹500 crore by midweek. That would leave it about ₹100 crore short of the original Jailer's lifetime total and roughly ₹150 crore behind 2.0, the incumbent Kollywood industry hit — with most of its run still ahead of it.

For diaspora audiences, the overseas split is the striking part: nearly half the worldwide gross so far has come from outside India, powered by the North America premiere run we reported earlier and packed shows in the Gulf and Southeast Asia. The critical reception has been cooler than the commercial one — critics praised Rajinikanth's swagger while faulting the plot, as our review roundup noted — but word of mouth among fans is plainly overriding it at the ticket window.

What to watch

Saturday's advance bookings are the next tell. If day three matches or beats day two — common for event films riding a holiday weekend — Jailer 2 stops being a hit story and becomes a record chase: the biggest Kollywood grosser ever is suddenly a live possibility rather than trade-talk optimism.
